articles.title: SJAA Programs and Events
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a wide array of programs and events for both its members and the public. These include educational opportunities like Quick STARt and Astronomy 101, equipment support services such as the Telescope Fix-It and Loaner Programs, and various observing events including star parties (In-Town, School, Starry Nights), solar observing, and astro-imaging sessions. The association aims to support amateur astronomers of all levels, from beginners to those interested in specialized fields like astrophotography.

articles.title: Member Appreciation Night
articles.summary: SJAA hosted its annual Member Appreciation Night on February 15th, acknowledging the vital role of its volunteers in running the organization. Outstanding Service Awards were presented to George and Creighton Voon, Walter and Frances Yau, and Gary Mitchell for their significant contributions to various programs and events. The article also encourages members to engage in volunteering, highlighting diverse opportunities and the potential for employer matching grants for volunteer hours.

articles.title: Observe Jupiter Like Galileo
articles.summary: This article encourages readers to observe Jupiter's four largest moons (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto) using binoculars or a small telescope, emulating Galileo's pivotal observations from 1610. It details Galileo's early telescopic endeavors, his observational challenges, and how his discoveries supported the heliocentric theory. The piece provides practical advice for modern amateur astronomers to sketch their observations and identify the moons.

articles.title: KIDS CORNER
articles.summary: This 'KIDS CORNER' article presents an engaging word search puzzle featuring various galaxy names like Milky Way, Andromeda, and Whirlpool. It also provides fun and educational facts about galaxies, focusing on the Milky Way's etymology, immense size (87,000 light-years across), mass (1.5 trillion solar masses), and estimated planetary count (at least 100 billion planets). The content is designed to be informative and entertaining for a younger audience.

articles.title: Elections and Appointments
articles.summary: The article details the recent annual board member elections, held between February 8th and 15th, which saw Ken Miura, Swami Nigam, and Marianne Damon re-elected, and Larry Zurbrick replacing Vini Carter. It also covers new board appointments, including Carl Svensson as Vice President, Chris Gotthrath in Speaker and Volunteer Chair roles, and Steven Green leading the Mendoza Ranch program. Furthermore, the organization reported an increase in membership while noting changes in its social media follower counts.

articles.title: Spring Swap Meet 2025
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) has announced its Spring Swap Meet for Sunday, March 16, 2025, from 9 AM to noon at Houge Park in San Jose. This casual event is designed for the local amateur astronomy community to buy, sell, or trade used astronomical equipment with minimal overhead, building on the success of a previous swap meet.

articles.title: Model for Gravitational Lensing
articles.summary: Bogdan Szafraniec's paper, published in the American Journal of Physics, proposes a simplified optics equation to model gravitational lensing, making this complex phenomenon more accessible to students without requiring a deep understanding of general relativity. Drawing on Fermat's principle and the Euler equation, the model describes light bending, reflection, and looping, and can reproduce observed features like Einstein rings. The authors hope this intuitive approach will encourage more students to explore general relativity and seek simple solutions to complex problems.

articles.title: The View from Below the Skies
articles.summary: The article discusses the evolution of Amateur Telescope Making (ATM), noting a shift from traditional scratch-building to modern methods leveraging 3D printing, open-source software, and single-board computers. While classic ATM has waned due to affordable commercial optics, a 'new golden age' of DIY astronomy is emerging with accessible technology. The author, President of SJAA, encourages members to engage in these new forms of ATM through club events and project discussions.

articles.title: Board Minutes
articles.summary: The SJAA board minutes from late 2024 to early 2025 detail several key organizational activities, including the approval of the 2025 calendar and an ongoing discussion regarding a potential membership fee increase. Key operational items covered were reporting requirements for the San Jose Parks Department and efforts to advance the 24" Dob Task Force. Additionally, the board planned for outreach events like the Santa Cruz STEAM Expo and collaborations with Astro Revolution, while also evaluating the integration of Discord for club communications.

articles.title: Planetary Parade
articles.summary: The article details a "grand alignment" or "planetary parade" of all major Solar System planets that occurred in January and February, making them simultaneously visible. It explains the scientific reason behind such alignments, attributing it to the planets' shared orbital plane, and showcases astrophotography by SJAA members featuring the Sun, Jupiter, Mars, and Venus, often with details about the equipment and techniques employed.
